variants.name: Servlet Filter chain (jakarta.servlet)
variants.implementation_notes: The servlet container owns the intercepting layer: implement Filter#doFilter(ServletRequest, ServletResponse, FilterChain), validate (and optionally wrap) the request, and call `chain.doFilter(...)` only when it passes - omitting the call is the rejection, which the container API documents as the canonical filter behaviour. Register the filter for all URL patterns (`/*` or @WebFilter) so no route bypasses it, and keep rule logic in shared validator classes or jakarta.validation constraints so the same rules serve controllers.
pitfalls: A filter mapped only to selected URL patterns, or a servlet reached through another dispatcher, voids complete coverage; map once to /* and assert it in tests.
doFilter runs on container threads; validator state must be stateless or thread-safe, and container-created filters cannot rely on CDI/Spring injection without registration beans.
Wrapping the request to sanitise it changes what downstream code sees; wrap deliberately and keep one canonical request representation.

variants.name: Spring MVC declarative Bean Validation (@Valid)
variants.implementation_notes: Spring registers a global Validator (LocalValidatorFactoryBean, backed by Hibernate Validator when present) and validates @Valid/@Validated controller method arguments before the handler runs; constraints are declared declaratively on the model, and MethodValidationPostProcessor extends the same mechanism to @Validated service methods. This replaces hand-written interceptor classes for body-shaped validation; the container-level filter still owns envelope checks (sizes, encodings, headers) because Bean Validation runs only after the message converter has parsed the body.
pitfalls: Only annotated endpoints are validated: a new handler without @Valid is silently unvalidated, so pin coverage with tests over the request mappings.
Body validation happens after parsing, so oversized or malformed payloads can fail in the converter with a different status than a constraint violation; handle both paths in the error contract.
Method validation uses AOP proxies: self-invocation inside a bean bypasses the proxy and therefore the validation.
